content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes or positive sentiment; model tends to overshoot in bullish phases.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or shows strong downward momentum; model fails to adjust downward quickly.
- Lag in correction: model often delays reacting to sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment turns negative.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to revert to historical mean when sentiment weakens.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early phases of positive sentiment, then overly pessimistic in late phases.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., >0.11), model overestimates; if consistently negative (e.g., < -0.2), model underestimates.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends; model often assumes trend continuation when sentiment suggests reversal.
